videos.title: Turn SQL into tools
videos.short: PlumeSQL in a minute and a half
videos.summary: PlumeSQL is a desktop IDE for PostgreSQL where a SQL file can become a monitor, a dashboard or a button. In a minute and a half: connections found in your project files, completion that reads CTEs and subqueries, PL/pgSQL checked against your server before anything is created, an object tree that sees your own open transaction, a SQL file with a few comments that becomes a live lock monitor with a Terminate button, charts from the extensions Marketplace, and VS Code's editor and keys. Free, no account, for macOS, Windows and Linux.

videos.summary: PlumeSQL's SQL editor completes what your statement actually defines, not just the tables in the database. The Outline beside the editor lists every statement and the objects it touches: a click finds an object in the script, a double click opens its definition. Run executes the statement under the cursor: the first press selects it, the second runs it.

videos.title: FROM-first queries (experimental)
videos.short: Write the FROM first and the columns complete as you type (experimental).
videos.summary: PlumeSQL can let you write a query in the order it runs, FROM first. It is experimental and off by default: switch it on in Settings, Experimental, FROM-first queries (editor.fromFirst). The semicolon, Run and Explain write the query back as standard SQL, so the server only ever sees SQL, and one undo gives your own order back.

videos.title: Key joins: joins read from your foreign keys
videos.short: Joins written from your foreign keys, and a warning when a join repeats the rows you sum.
videos.summary: PlumeSQL writes your joins from the foreign keys: name the table and its ON or USING is offered, or type join and every table the keys reach comes with its whole condition. It also reads every join against the keys of its tables, the idea the Key Joins proposal makes a guarantee of: a join on a unique key keeps each row once, any other may repeat them. A one-to-many join gets a quiet hint, and a sum or count over rows a join repeats gets a warning before you run it. Here a customer's rentals counted and payments summed through two such joins say 960 rentals instead of 32, and summing the payments in a subquery fixes it.

The fix: drop that join, sum the payments in a subquery
No warnings left; the quiet hint on rental stays
Run it again: 32 rentals and 114.70, the real numbers
